      "partial_result": "## Verdict: ACCEPT, with no blockers\n\nThe frozen driver is safe to freeze and run once on the authenticated original bytes, as a six-file source fragment only. It does not accept anything for serving, native, quality or speed, and the FULL KILL stands.\n\nI reviewed the frozen snapshot only; its hashes match `snapshot.json` (driver `92e15610\u2026`, test `3359b8a0\u2026`). The four helpers match the DGX compile pins (`3c80a7be` / `0e552eb8` / `d361dd46` / `ee0870e4`) and haven't changed between `10e0b370` and HEAD. The worker files aren't in this worktree. I edited no repo or worker files.\n\n**Both of your earlier fixes are in the snapshot:**\n- **Failure-path rehash:** `run()` now starts its `finally` with an unconditional `fresh()` loop over every captured file (`qualify_connected_gallery_fragment.py:552-553`). That covers failures in capture, conversion, verification and publication, and the original error stays primary through `add_note` (`:482-490`). `test_failed_converter_and_publisher_still_fresh_check_every_capture` checks it.\n- **Measured cost:** the final deadline check, `elapsed_seconds` and `peak_rss_bytes` come after the whole cleanup (`:575-577`). `test_report_measurements_include_fresh_exit_checks` shows they include the exit rehash.\n\n**Every item on your checklist holds:**\n- **Authority:** its raw SHA is checked through a no-follow descriptor before parsing (`:494-495`, `:152-156`). Parsing rejects duplicate keys and non-finite numbers, and the schema check requires exact keys and real ints, so booleans fail (`:88-89`, `:240-275`).\n- **Pins before any package code runs:** the driver, test, four sources, interpreter and four inputs are all hash-checked (`:494-498`) before `modules.load` (`:501`).\n- **Package source:** compiled from the captured bytes with no `.pyc`, and the finder refuses any `sfora` module that wasn't captured (`:195-197`, `:217-220`). The module registry holds exactly four entries and never removes a foreign one (`:199-237`).\n- **Converter:** called exactly once (`:503`).\n- **Checks before mkdir** (`verify_members`, `:278-380`, then fresh rehash at `:514-515`, then `Output` at `:517`):\n  - every selected 130-byte row is compared by `os.pread` against the original wire at its ordinal;\n  - ID order, the B32-plus-tail batch shape and the external reference are checked;\n  - the three original files must be identical to the inputs;\n  - `producer.gallery_wire_sha256` must be `None`.\n- **No mismatch with the binder:** `verify_members` rebuilds `identity`, `combined_wire`, `gallery_batches`, `gallery_rows` and the strictly ascending ordinals exactly as `bind_gallery_provenance` does. The reference script hashes IDs with the same canonical encoding, so the real run shouldn't fail on an encoding difference.\n- **Publication** uses the genuine `publish_bytes_noreplace`. Each member's file descriptor stays open until a final readback that checks inode identity, link count 1, size, bytes, SHA and the exact six-file inventory (`:422-440`). Directory identity is re-checked around each write (`:410-420`).\n- **Cleanup** removes only files and the directory it can match by inode identity (`:442-467`).\n- **Limits:** the 1 GiB address-space cap and the alarm are set before any real work (`:605-609`).\n- **Success** is reported only as exit 0 plus one canonical JSON line (`:619-622`).\n- **Input sizes** all fit the 16 MiB per-file read cap: receipt 6.18 MB, bundle 547 KB, owner audit 968 KB, wire 448,370 B.\n\n## Checks to do before the one run (environment, not source)\n\n1. **The output's parent directory must not be setgid.** `Output.guard` requires the new directory's mode to be exactly `0o700`, but a setgid parent makes it `0o2700`. I reproduced this with a tiny stdlib test (`0o2700 False`). The run would fail cleanly right after mkdir, which still uses up the one authorized run. Check with `stat -c %a <parent>`.\n2. **The output filesystem must support `O_TMPFILE` and `linkat`** through `/proc/self/fd`, because the existing publisher uses both. ext4, xfs or tmpfs are fine; avoid NFS.\n3. **Canonical paths for everything.** The owner audit (`8e38d2e5\u2026`) still has `remote_path: null`, so it needs staging on the DGX at a path with no symlinks. Invoke exactly `/usr/bin/python3.12 -I -S -B <abs driver> --authority <abs> --authority-sha256 <sha>`.\n4. **The parent's acceptance check must be strict.** The test's `parent_accepts` only re-reads the member files. The real parent should also match the report's `authority`, `sources`, `inputs` and `python` against the frozen authority, and `observed` against 1715 / `386f3b22\u2026` / `df9fb988\u2026`. Exit 0 can happen without success: `--help`, or any `SystemExit(0)` that escapes.\n\n## Should-fix (doesn't block the run)\n\n- **The alarm can escape cleanup** (`:551-572`, `:581-582`). The timer stays armed during `finally`. If it fires between two cleanup steps rather than inside one, the `TimeoutError` skips the rest of cleanup and replaces the original error. A complete six-file directory can then survive with exit 1. That stays diagnostic-only under the contract, and real runtime is seconds against a 120 s budget.\n  - Minimal repair: call `signal.pthread_sigmask(signal.SIG_BLOCK, {signal.SIGALRM})` at the start of `finally` and keep the explicit deadline check there.\n  - Discriminating test: on a successful in-process run, use `sys.settrace` to call `signal.raise_signal(SIGALRM)` on the `modules.close` line. Today the output survives; after the repair it is removed.\n- **A late deadline also leaves survivors.** If the deadline check at `:575` or `:620` fails after cleanup has finished, the outputs stay with exit 1.
